lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Cut the card-dispute form's abandonment rate from 37% to 22% in a four-week A/B test by splitting it into three short steps with saved progress.
- Ran 18 moderated usability sessions a quarter from a recruiting panel of 400 customers, so every major release was tested with real account holders before launch.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Raised the onboarding flow's System Usability Scale score from 68 to 104 across two rounds of moderated testing with 20 customers.
- Validated the redesigned app navigation's findability with an open card sort of 30 customers before it shipped.
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Apr 2020 - Feb 2022
- Ran the monthly patient survey and rebuilt its reporting dashboard, cutting the time from survey close to published findings from 3 weeks to 4 days.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Wrote the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Championed an inclusive, human-centered design approach to transit wayfinding that delivered meaningful, user-first outcomes.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Redesigned a free clinic's online booking flow, cutting the steps to book from 9 to 4; phone bookings fell by a quarter in the next two months.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA)
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interveiws, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: The résumé includes a date of birth and nationality that readers are not meant to weigh.
items.because: These details do not help readers assess qualifications and can distract from experience and skills.

items.says: Education appears before Experience and Projects despite several years of relevant professional experience.
items.because: That ordering delays the strongest evidence of experience.

items.says: The résumé shows a 10-month period with no study or work listed between May 2019 and April 2020.
The final clause is a lengthy, broad rationale that distracts from the session and panel details.
“Synthesizing” is the wrong tense for this ended role and does not match “cut.”
items.because: The role ended in June 2025, so the participle makes the action sound ongoing and interrupts the past-tense result.

items.says: The long list of inputs and methods delays the 23% result.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the clearest evidence of the work’s value.

items.says: The reported SUS score of 104 is invalid.
items.because: Standard SUS scores run from 0 to 100.

items.says: An open card sort cannot by itself validate navigation findability.
items.because: It shows how participants group and label content, not whether they can find items in a navigation structure.

items.says: The line claims findability validation without giving a card-sort finding or other evidence for it.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what result showed that the navigation was findable.

items.says: The sign-up result is delayed behind the prototype-testing detail.
items.because: The increase in completed sign-ups is the most direct evidence of impact and would be easier to spot first.

items.says: The missed-appointment result is delayed behind the interview and reminder details.
items.because: A reader scanning the experience may move on before reaching the clearest evidence of impact.

items.says: The line does not name the kind of test or the period used to measure the call reduction.
The broad design-language claim does not identify the work or a checkable user outcome.
items.because: It does not show what shaped the map or say what became easier or better.

items.says: The line names a design philosophy rather than the design work performed.
The reduction from 90 to 60 seconds is a 33.3% decrease, not a 50% improvement.
items.because: The time fell by 30 seconds from a starting point of 90 seconds.

items.says: The strongest project result is not the opening bullet.
items.because: The route-finding result is more concrete and compelling than the broad opening claim.

items.says: The line does not say whose performance the median represents or what test produced the times.
The change from 65% to 85% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% relative increase.
items.because: Relative to the starting 65%, the increase is about 30.8%.

items.says: The line does not specify the task participants completed or what counted as success.
items.because: Without that context, a reader cannot tell what the result demonstrates.

items.says: The audio landmarks and high-contrast colors repeat the method stated in the preceding bullet.
The phone-booking decline has no stated comparison period.
“The steps to book” is redundant with “booking flow.”
The clause about six issues makes the outcome harder to scan than a compact statement of what was fixed.
The handbook’s later use is buried in a lengthy trailing clause.
“interveiws” is misspelled.
items.because: The visible typo can distract from the methods listed and creates a preventable polish issue.
